supporting_observations.claim: Two domain logon failures for noah.kim occurred about 94 seconds apart. Both report an incorrect-password status and the same source address, 198.51.100.201.

About 89 seconds after the second failure, a network logon for noah.kim succeeded, reporting the same source address. This sequence is suspicious and consistent with failed password attempts followed by successful credential use, but does not by itself establish malicious activity.
The authentication records identify the source as an IP address rather than a named workstation, so the available records do not tie the logons to an approved organizational host.

known_telemetry_limitations: The authentication records do not identify the device or person using the reported source address.
The reported address, 198.51.100.201, is in a documentation-only address range; it cannot establish a real-world source location or ownership.
No network-flow, firewall, endpoint process, or session telemetry is provided to corroborate the logons or show what happened after the successful authentication.
The available records show only two failures in the reviewed interval, which is not enough to determine whether they reflect password guessing or a legitimate user error.
claims_not_established: Whether the successful logon was authorized or performed by noah.kim.
Whether the failures were malicious password guessing or ordinary incorrect password attempts.
The actual device or network that originated the authentication attempts.
Whether the successful session accessed resources or performed suspicious actions.
additional_evidence_needed: Verify with noah.kim whether they attempted to log on around 13:42–13:46 UTC and whether they recognize the source device.
Correlate the source address with firewall, NAT, DHCP, and network-flow records, accounting for possible address sanitization.
Review domain-controller authentication and session records, including related logons and resource access, for the same account and time window.
Collect endpoint telemetry from any device identified as the source and from WS-NKIM-01 for corroborating activity.
